evidence:
tls.lisp:959-961
(defun fnn-tls-ssc-fail (what)
  (error 'fnn-tls-unavailable
         :detail (format nil "~a failed~@[: ~a~]" what (first (fnn-tls-error-stack)))))
fnn-tls-error-stack (282-289) returns a string, either `(format nil "~{~a~^; ~}" ...)` or "OpenSSL reported no queued detail".
fix: Use the string directly, `(fnn-tls-error-stack)`, without FIRST.
reviewer: fnn-tls-error-stack (tls.lisp:282-289) always returns a string. fnn-tls-ssc-fail (tls.lisp:959-961) calls (first <string>), which signals TYPE-ERROR in SBCL, so fnn-tls-unavailable is never built. The only caller path is operator.lisp:156 through fnn-operator-execute-tls-self-signed (operator.lisp:161-173). That handler catches every error and maps it with fnn-exit-code-for, so this is not an unhandled crash. The real effect is that the exit and status are classified from a TYPE-ERROR rather than as tls-unavailable, and the OpenSSL reason is lost. This only happens when OpenSSL fails during self-signed generation.
scenario: Any failure while generating the self-signed key or certificate (EVP_PKEY_keygen, RAND_bytes, EVP_DigestSignFinal, i2d_*; 12 call sites) evaluates (first "..."), which signals TYPE-ERROR before fnn-tls-unavailable is constructed. The operator gets "The value ... is not of type LIST" instead of the OpenSSL reason. A caller that handles fnn-tls-error or fnn-tls-unavailable to report a refused generation misses the condition, so a library failure becomes an unclassified host crash.
title: fnn-tls-ssc-fail calls FIRST on a string, so every self-signed failure becomes a TYPE-ERROR
